stem.text: Find the value of \( \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\ln(1 + x) - x}{x^{2} + x^{3}} \).

worked_solution.text: As \( x \to 0 \), the numerator \( \ln(1 + x) - x \) tends to \( 0 \).
As \( x \to 0 \), the denominator \( x^{2} + x^{3} \) tends to \( 0 \).

The numerator and the denominator both tend to 0, so the form is \( \frac{0}{0} \) and L'Hospital's rule applies. Differentiate the numerator and the denominator separately: the limit equals \( \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\frac{1}{1 + x} - 1}{2x + 3x^{2}} \).

The new numerator and denominator both tend to 0 again, so the form is still \( \frac{0}{0} \) and the rule applies once more. Differentiate each separately again: the limit equals \( \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{-\frac{1}{(1 + x)^{2}}}{2 + 6x} \).
At \( x = 0 \) this numerator is \( -1 \) and this denominator is \( 2 \), which is not 0, so the limit is \( - \frac{1}{2} \).
